<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Datasets and Experimental Details</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Galaxea Open-World Dataset</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We train on the Galaxea Open-World Dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jiang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, a large-scale real-world mobile-manipulation dataset with <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>500 hours of demonstrations (about 100K trajectories). The dataset spans 150 task categories across 50 real-world scenes and covers more than 1,600 objects and 58 skills. Importantly for our setting, data are collected under a single consistent embodiment, so that perception streams, action/state signals, and language annotations are naturally aligned for end-to-end VLA training.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Platform.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All demonstrations are recorded on the Galaxea R1 Lite platform, which is also the real robot we use for our zero-shot evaluation in Sec. <a href="#S4" title="4 Evaluation ‣ SimVLA: A Simple VLA Baseline for Robotic Manipulation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. R1 Lite is a mobile bimanual robot with a 23-DoF embodiment (two 6-DoF arms, a 3-DoF torso for workspace extension, a 6-DoF vector-drive omnidirectional base up to 1.5 m/s, and two 1-DoF grippers). The platform is equipped with a head stereo RGB camera for scene-level context and dual Intel RealSense D405 RGB-D wrist cameras for close-range manipulation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Real-robot evaluation details</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each real-robot task, we use a simple rubric that measures whether the policy can complete the task within the fixed time budget used in Sec. <a href="#S4" title="4 Evaluation ‣ SimVLA: A Simple VLA Baseline for Robotic Manipulation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. We report binary success/failure over 50 trials.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Store the dolls.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The robot must pick up <span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">three</span> plush dolls placed on a tabletop and put them into a designated storage container. Success is defined as all three dolls being fully inside the container at the end of the episode.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Arrange eggs.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The robot must pick up <span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">one</span> egg and place it into a designated slot of an egg carton. Success is defined as the egg being seated in the target slot without being dropped.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Put the flowers in the vase.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The robot must grasp a flower and insert it into the opening of a vase. Success is defined as the flower being inside the vase and remaining stably placed at the end of the episode.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Put the pen into the pen holder.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The robot must pick up <span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">two</span> pens and insert them into a pen holder. Success is defined as both pens being inside the holder (stably contained) at the end of the episode.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Wipe the desktop.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The robot must wipe a visible stain/dirty region on a desktop using a <span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">cloth rag</span>. Success is defined as the target region being visibly cleaned (stain disappears or is substantially reduced) within the time budget.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Fold the clothes.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The robot must fold a shirt starting from a flat or mildly wrinkled state on the table. Success is defined as completing the target fold (folding in sleeves and making a main fold) with the garment remaining on the working surface.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px7" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Pick up garbage on the ground.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The robot must pick up <span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">two</span> plastic bottles from the ground and dispose them into a trash bin. Success is defined as both bottles ending inside the bin.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px8" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Open the drawer.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The robot must grasp the drawer handle and pull to open the drawer to a specified extent. Success is defined as the drawer being opened beyond a threshold without damaging the mechanism.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Training hyperparameters</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To facilitate reproducibility, we summarize the key hyperparameters used in our simulation training (LIBERO) and real-robot training (Galaxea-500h). All simulation runs are executed on <span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">4<math id="A1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>H100</span> GPUs and are initialized from a pretrained VLM backbone (without any VLA data pretraining).
For complete implementation details, please refer to our codebase on the project website.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Simulation.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A1.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ Simulation. ‣ A.3 Training hyperparameters ‣ Appendix A Datasets and Experimental Details ‣ SimVLA: A Simple VLA Baseline for Robotic Manipulation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> reports the configuration.</p>
</div>

<section id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Real-robot training (Galaxea-500h).</h5>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A1.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ Real-robot training (Galaxea-500h). ‣ A.3 Training hyperparameters ‣ Appendix A Datasets and Experimental Details ‣ SimVLA: A Simple VLA Baseline for Robotic Manipulation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> summarizes the training setup on the Galaxea Open-World Dataset. For a fair comparison, both our method and <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0.5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0.5</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0.5}</annotation></semantics></math> are trained using the same Galaxea data and the same hyperparameters, with the same compute budget: <span id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">64<math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>H100</span> GPUs for <span id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">150K</span> training steps.</p>

              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
